ANCHORED ON THE LAB CONTROLS, 2026-11-24, and re-described. It is NOT a shape test: measured over db2's 430,820 candidates, every row it alone rejects has redundancy >= 0.534 and every row the coverage floor alone rejects has redundancy <= 0.480, so the two partition at r = 0.51 with no overlap and saturation only ever acts where 1-exp(-r) has gone to 1 and it IS coverage. Read correctly it is a DEPTH-NORMALISED abundance floor: 5% of what the depth allowed, which is a lower bar on a shallow library and a flat 5% at full depth. What anchors the level is the pure-fungal control set, where the true organism is known: across 16 spore and axenic-culture runs the four artefacts (all congeners of the true organism) reach coverage 0.0200, 0.0236, 0.0311 and 0.0336, while the nine true organisms sit at 0.175 to 0.463. The coverage floor of 0.02 admits all four artefacts; this floor excludes all four. n is four, which is small, and it is ground truth, which the previous basis (a percentile of what db_v3's retired score called real) was not. The genuine shape question, where in a transcript the reads fell, needs positions and is release/04_align's.

below this the saturation statistic is silent and the call rests on the two floors. For small x, 1-exp(-x) is approximately x, so coverage approximates redundancy mechanically and everything scores near 1

a detection with more than 80% of its reads under one sub-species node is LCA smearing, not a genome-wide infection. Neither arm contains a single sub-species node, so fsp_frac is 0 on every candidate and the test never fires. Retained because admitting one strain-level assembly makes it live again

ANCHORED ON THE LAB CONTROLS, 2026-11-25. The host is RANKED and not thresholded -- every plant library has a host, so the question is which plant, not whether -- but a pure fungal library has no host at all and ranking alone still named one: in the spore control SRR6043971 Triticum aestivum was called at coverage 0.0018, cross-mapping only. This floor asks the prior question, is there any plant in this library, and the rank picks the winner among those that pass. The level is the lowest host coverage in any control library KNOWN to contain host tissue: across 86 curated lab runs, the 70 where host is expected (infected_tissue, host_only, haustoria) span 0.0066 to 0.3185 and the 16 where it is not (spores, axenic_culture) span 0.0000 to 0.0252. A floor at 0.0066 is the minimum-error point over that set: it loses 0 of the 70 real hosts and still admits 2 of the 16 that should have none. It is deliberately permissive -- a missing host call costs this chapter more than a weak one, and the host is not part of any detection claim. Evidence: data/curation/lab_material.tsv
